verses.73:1: Por que, Deus, {repulisti} {f1}: * {v1join} o vosso furor contra as ovelhas da vossa pastagem?
verses.73:2: Lembrai-vos da vossa {congregatio}, * que {possedisti} desde o início.
verses.73:2b: Resgatastes a {virga} da vossa herança: * o monte Sião, em que habitastes.
verses.73:3: Levantai as vossas mãos contra {superbias} {f3}: * quanto mal fez o inimigo {insancto}!
verses.73:4: E se gloriaram os que vos odeiam: * no meio da vossa {solemnitas}.
verses.73:5: Puseram {s5}: * e não {cognoverunt}, como na saída, {summum}.
verses.73:6: Como numa selva de árvores, com machados cortaram as suas portas {idipsum}: * com machado e {ascia} a derrubaram.
verses.73:7: {incenderunt} vosso santuário: * na terra {polluerunt} a tenda do vosso nome.
verses.73:8: Disseram no seu coração, {cognatio}: * Façamos cessar da terra todos os {diesfestos} de Deus.
verses.73:9: Não vimos {s9}, já não há profeta: * e {amplius}.
verses.73:10: Até quando, Deus, {imp10} o inimigo: * o adversário {irr10} o vosso nome {f10}?
verses.73:11: Por que {avertis} a vossa mão, e a vossa direita, * do meio do vosso seio {f11}?
verses.73:12: {v12} antes dos séculos: * operou a salvação no meio da terra.
verses.73:13: Vós {confirmasti} o mar com o vosso poder: * {contribulasti} as cabeças dos dragões nas águas.
verses.73:14: Vós quebrastes as cabeças do dragão: * {dedisti} aos povos dos etíopes.
verses.73:15: Vós rompestes fontes e torrentes: * vós secastes os rios de Etã.
verses.73:16: Vosso é o dia, e vossa é a noite: * vós {fabricatus} a aurora e o sol.
verses.73:17: Vós fizestes todos os limites da terra: * o verão e a primavera, vós os moldastes.
verses.73:18: Lembrai-vos disto: o inimigo {imp18} o Senhor, * e um povo insensato {inc18} o vosso nome.
verses.73:19: Não entregueis às feras as almas {confitentes}, * e não esqueçais {f19} as almas dos vossos pobres.
verses.73:20: Olhai para a vossa aliança: * porque {obscurati} estão cheios de casas de iniquidades.
verses.73:21: Que o humilde {avertatur}: * o pobre e o carente louvarão o vosso nome.
verses.73:22: Levantai-vos, Deus, julgai a vossa causa: * lembrai-vos das vossas {imp22}, {v22ab} o dia todo.
verses.73:23: Não esqueçais as vozes dos vossos inimigos: * a soberba dos que vos odeiam sobe sempre.

decisions.latin: Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem
decisions.why: The Latin verb has no object, and neither has the Greek (ἀπώσω). The verb is the settled *repelir* (repéllere without *a*, D42; 59:3 *vós nos repelistes*). *Repelir* is transitive, and a bare *repelistes* leaves the ear waiting for an object. The object the context gives is the people, the *ovelhas da vossa pastagem* of the next colon, so *nos* is supplied as a pronoun Portuguese needs (D2). Douay-Rheims supplies *us* and Matos Soares 1932 *nos* as well. The bare verb is the option for a reader who wants the Latin's silence kept. Two blind readers (Pss 42, 59) did not know *repelistes*. That is the row's known cost.

options.label: nos repelistes
options.note: Ruling: the object supplied (DRB *cast us off*, MS1932 *nos desamparaste*).

options.label: repelistes
options.note: The Latin's bare verb; the object is left unsaid.

options.label: nos desamparastes
options.note: MS1932's verb (the row's option); it gives up D42's *repelir*.

decisions.latin: irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
decisions.why: *Ut quid* governs both colons and the Latin simply goes on, with no conjunction. Portuguese cannot carry a *por que* over a colon break without help: bare *se irou o vosso furor…?* would be heard as a new statement. *E* carries the question over and adds no sense. Repeating *por que* (Douay-Rheims *why is thy wrath*, MS1932 *(Por que razão)* in his parenthesis) says the question twice where the Latin says it once. *irátus est furor* → *se irou o vosso furor*: the irásci row's verb, and the Latin's image of wrath growing angry. MS1932's *se acendeu* is the Hebrew's smoke.

options.label: por que se irou
options.note: Repeats the interrogative, as DRB and MS1932 do.

options.label: se irou
options.note: The Latin's asyndeton; heard as a statement.

decisions.latin: in finem (five times)
decisions.why: The *in finem* row (D27) says *para sempre* where the phrase means perpetuity and leaves each psalm to decide. Four places here do mean that: 73:1 *repelled for ever*, 73:10 the settled *Úsquequo … in finem* formula (*Até quando … para sempre?*), 73:11 and 73:19. 73:19 is a negation, and D27's failure at 9:19 was *não … até o fim*, which is why the row chose *para sempre*: *não esqueçais para sempre* is the settled form. 73:3 is the exception. *Levantai as vossas mãos … para sempre* would make God's lifted hands perpetual. There εἰς τέλος has the sense of 17:36b (*até o fim*: to the finish, utterly). Douay-Rheims has *unto the end* and MS1932 *sem limites*, which he attaches to the pride. *até o fim* at the end of the colon can still be heard with either the hands or the pride, as the Latin can.

options.label: para sempre ×4, até o fim at 73:3
options.note: Ruling: the row, with 17:36b's reading at 73:3.

options.label: para sempre everywhere
options.note: One Portuguese for the psalm's five; 73:3 is then heard as lifting the hands for ever.

options.label: até o fim everywhere
options.note: DRB's *unto the end* everywhere; breaks the settled formula at 73:10 and repeats 9:19's fault at 73:19.

decisions.latin: Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ
decisions.why: The Greek is συναγωγή, and D34 gives συναγωγή *congregação* (21:17; synagóga; the row *congregátio pópuli → congregação do povo*, 61:9). *Assembleia* is ecclésia's (D34). This colon lives alone in the liturgy: it is the Thursday antiphon *Memor esto * congregatiónis tuæ, Dómine, quam possedísti ab inítio* (Psalmi minor.txt, with Ps 73 in three parts) and the versicle of the Preces *V. Meménto Congregatiónis tuæ. R. Quam possedísti ab inítio* (Special/Preces.txt; Appendix/Psalmi graduales.txt). Found by grep. The blind reader of 61:9 heard *congregação* as the assembly. MS1932 has *família*, which interprets.

options.label: assembleia
options.note: ecclésia's word (D34); would merge two Latin words.

options.label: família
options.note: MS1932; interprets the gathering as kin.

decisions.latin: quam possedísti ab inítio
decisions.why: *possidére* → *possuir* is the working word of the open row (43:4). The Greek ἐκτήσω is 'acquired, got for yourself', and the Hebrew is the same. The Latin says *possessed*, and that is the word followed here (rule 1). Douay-Rheims has *possessed*, MS1932 *possuíste*. *ab inítio* → *desde o início* (the row *inítio · princípium*; 118:152 *Desde o início*).

options.label: adquiristes
options.note: The Greek's sense (ἐκτήσω), not the Latin's.

decisions.latin: Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ
decisions.why: *virga → vara* (row; 2:9, 44:7). ῥάβδον κληρονομίας: the Hebrew שֵׁבֶט is both rod and tribe, and the Latin chose the rod. Douay-Rheims has *sceptre* and MS1932 *cetro*, and both interpret. The row keeps the concrete staff. The blind reader of 44:7 heard sceptre in *vara* anyway. *redímere → resgatar* (row; 30:6, 70:23 *que resgatastes*).

options.label: cetro
options.note: DRB, MS1932; interprets the rod as royal.

options.label: tribo
options.note: The Hebrew's other sense; not the Latin's word. Refused.

decisions.latin: in supérbias eórum
decisions.why: The Latin plural (ὑπερηφανίας) stands here and the singular at 73:23 (*supérbia eórum*). The plural *as soberbas* can be said, but it is rare, and *soberbas* is also the feminine plural adjective 'proud'. Number is grammar (D2, D27): *a soberba* here as at 73:23, with the plural as the option. *deles*, not *sua*: after *as vossas mãos*, *sua* could be heard as the enemy's single *inimigo* or be left unclear (as 48:15b).

options.label: a soberba deles
options.note: Ruling: the singular (DRB *their pride*, MS1932 *a sua soberba*).

decisions.latin: quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
decisions.why: The row *sancta / sanctum (a place) → o lugar santo* (19:3, 21:4, 62:3), with the exception 59:8 *no seu santo*, where the bare neuter could mean the holy one or holiness. Here it is plainly a place: the verses that follow burn the sanctuary and cut down its doors. Douay-Rheims has *in the sanctuary*. *no santuário* would merge it with *sanctuárium* four verses later (73:7), which the row keeps apart. *malignári → fazer o mal* (row, 36:8–9). *quanta* is an exclamation, as 65:16 *quanto ele fez*.

options.label: no santo
options.note: 59:8's bare neuter; keeps it open where the context has already closed it.

decisions.latin: in médio solemnitátis tuæ … omnes dies festos Dei
decisions.why: Two Latin words for the feast: *solémnitas* (73:4) and *dies festi* (73:8). Behind both is one Greek, ἑορτή. D15's test would allow one Portuguese word, but Portuguese has a pair that says each Latin word exactly, so the Latin's variation is kept at no cost. *solenidade* is Douay-Rheims's *solemnity* and MS1932's word. *dias de festa* is MS1932's. The row *dies solémnis → dia solene* (117:27b) is kin.

options.label: festa … dias de festa
options.note: The Greek's one word; plainer at 73:4.

decisions.latin: Posuérunt signa sua, signa … Signa nostra non vídimus
decisions.why: The crux of the psalm. *signa* is a military ensign and a sign, and the Latin uses one word both times, and elsewhere for God's signs (64:9 *a signis tuis* → *os vossos sinais*). At 73:9 the lament beside *já não há profeta* wants signs, not flags. So one word for both places: *sinais*. *signa sua, signa* is predicative, as the Greek shows (ἔθεντο τὰ σημεῖα αὐτῶν σημεῖα: they set their signs up as signs), so *como* is supplied (grammar) and the repetition is kept. Douay-Rheims has *their ensigns for signs*. MS1932 has *os seus estandartes como troféus*, and *troféus* is his own. The bare Latin *os seus sinais, sinais* is an option.

options.label: os seus sinais como sinais / os nossos sinais
options.note: Ruling: one word for signa in both verses; the repetition kept.

options.label: os seus estandartes como sinais / os nossos estandartes
options.note: DRB *ensigns*, MS1932 *estandartes*; splits the one Latin word at 73:5 and makes 73:9 flags.

decisions.latin: et non cognovérunt
decisions.why: No object in the Latin, the Greek (καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν) or Douay-Rheims (*they knew not*). *conhecer* asks for an object in Portuguese. The row (13:4 *Não hão de saber todos*) gives *saber* where *cognóscere* stands alone. Here that keeps the Latin's objectless knowing. 73:9 *nos non cognóscet* has an object and keeps *conhecer*.

options.label: souberam
options.note: Ruling: the row's *saber* without an object.

options.label: conheceram
options.note: The row's verb; the ear waits for an object.

decisions.latin: sicut in éxitu super summum
decisions.why: The Latin is obscure and is left obscure. *In éxitu* ('in the going out') stands where the Greek has εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον, the entry, and the Latin is followed (rule 1). *éxitus → saída* (64:8, 67:21). *super summum* is 'on the top, above the highest part'. The row *summus* has *extremo* for the end of the sky (18:6b–7b) and names this place. Here it is a height (the top of a gateway?), not an end, so *cimo*. The row noted that *cimo* is heard as a mountain's, and that is a height too. Douay-Rheims has *on the highest top*. MS1932 reworks the phrase (*nem as eminências nem as saídas*).

options.label: sobre o extremo
options.note: 18:6b–7b's word; heard as an end, not a height.

decisions.latin: excidérunt jánuas ejus in idípsum … cognátio eórum simul
decisions.why: *in idípsum* (D9, deferred): the row's proposal is *juntos* for persons acting together (33:4, 61:10) and *a um só tempo* for one agent or a thing (4:9). Here the axemen are many, so *juntos*. It also matches 73:8, where *simul* (row → *juntos*) is the same Greek, ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό in both verses. So the psalm's two Latin words for one Greek are said alike, as D15's test allows. Douay-Rheims has *at once* (73:6) and *together* (73:8). MS1932 has *à porfia*, which is his own.

decisions.latin: in secúri et áscia
decisions.why: Two tools. *secúris* is the axe (*machados* in the first colon, *machado* here), and *áscia* is 'an axe for hewing wood, a carpenter's axe'. Lewis & Short cite this very verse. The Portuguese carpenter's hewing tool is the *enxó*. *machadinha* (Douay-Rheims *hatchet*) is plainer but repeats *machado*'s root, which the Latin does not. MS1932's *martelo* is another tool. Without articles, as the Latin has none. The blind reader should say whether *enxó* is known.

decisions.latin: Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum
decisions.why: The Latin says the fire twice (*incéndere* + *igni*), as the Greek does (ἐνεπύρισαν ἐν πυρί). *Atear fogo a* is the Portuguese idiom that keeps both: a verb of setting on fire, and *fogo*. *Incendiaram com fogo* is the cognate, with its pleonasm laid bare. *sanctuárium → santuário*, kept apart from *in sancto → no lugar santo* (row).

options.label: Incendiaram com fogo
options.note: The cognate; the doubling is heard as a fault in Portuguese.

decisions.latin: in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui
decisions.why: *pollúere* stands in the psalms only here and at 78:1 (*polluérunt templum sanctum tuum*). Its adjective 17:31 *impollúta* is already *Imaculado*, so *macular* keeps the family. *profanar* (Douay-Rheims *defiled*, MS1932 *profanaram*) is wanted for the Latin's own *profanáre* (88:32, 88:35). *contaminar* is contamináre's (D44, 54:21). That word has the same Greek (βεβηλόω), so D15's test would allow it here too; the option. *in terra* is kept as *na terra* (the Greek has 'to the ground'). *tabernáculum → tenda* (row).

options.label: contaminaram
options.note: contamináre's word (54:21), the same Greek verb.

decisions.latin: Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul
decisions.why: A collective singular subject (*cognátio*, 'kindred') with a plural verb and *simul*. Portuguese will not say *Disseram … a parentela deles* without strain. *os da parentela deles* makes the subject plural (MS1932 builds it so: *com os das suas parentelas*). *juntos* is simul's row word, and matches 73:6 (decision `idipsum`). *deles* keeps *eórum* apart from *suo* (their own heart).

options.label: juntos, os da parentela deles
options.note: Ruling: the subject made plural; *simul* kept.

options.label: a sua parentela, juntos
options.note: Word for word; *sua* may be heard as God's.

decisions.latin: et nos non cognóscet ámplius
decisions.why: The verse has *jam non* and, later, *non … ámplius*. The row *ámplius non → já não* (38:14) would say *já não* twice where the Latin varies. So *não … mais* here. The subject of *cognóscet* is not named (God? a prophet?), and Portuguese leaves it unnamed too. MS1932 names it *(Deus)* in a parenthesis.

options.label: não nos conhecerá mais
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's two adverbs kept two.

decisions.latin: improperábit inimícus … inimícus improperávit Dómino … improperiórum tuórum
decisions.why: *improperáre / impropérium* occur in the psalms only in this psalm (grep). The Greek is ὀνειδίζω / ὀνειδισμός, the Greek of *exprobráre / oppróbrium*, and that row has *afrontar / afronta* (68:10, 41:11 *afrontaram-me*, 38:9). By D15's test one Greek verb takes one Portuguese: *afrontar*, three times, as the Latin repeats it. *insultar* is obloqui's (43:17, D43). MS1932's *ultrajar* is the option. At 73:10 the verb has no object (as Douay-Rheims *shall the enemy reproach*). MS1932 adds *nos*.

options.label: afrontará / afrontou / afrontas
options.note: Ruling: the oppróbrium row, by the Greek.

decisions.latin: irrítat adversárius nomen tuum … incitávit nomen tuum
decisions.why: *irritáre* with God as object → *provocar* (settled, D27). *incitávit* in 73:18 is another Latin verb, but the same Greek (παρώξυνεν, as 73:10's παροξυνεῖ), and D27 already merged exacerbáre with irritáre on exactly that ground. So *provocar* both times: the name of God provoked, twice. Douay-Rheims has *provoke* in both. *irrítat* is a present, where the Greek has a future: the present is kept (rule 1), and the future is an option.

options.label: provoca / provocou
options.note: Ruling: D27; the Latin's present at 73:10.

options.label: provoca / incitou
options.note: The Latin's second verb kept apart; *incitar o vosso nome* is heard as urging it on.

decisions.latin: Ut quid avértis manum tuam
decisions.why: *avértere → desviar* (row; *desviais de mim a vossa face*, 12:1). Here it is used of the hand held back in the bosom. *retirar* (MS1932 *retrais*) says the image more plainly but leaves the row. Douay-Rheims has *turn away*.

decisions.latin: Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula
decisions.why: A verbless colon. Douay-Rheims reads it as a sentence (*But God is our king before ages*). MS1932 reads it as the subject of *operou* (*Mas Deus, que é nosso rei antes dos séculos, operou*). The copula is supplied (D2), with a full sentence at the mediant, and *operou* keeps God as its subject. The apposition is the option. *ante sǽcula → antes dos séculos* (DRB, MS1932). *operári → operar* (D43, which names this verse). *salus → salvação* (D6).

options.label: Mas Deus é o nosso Rei

forms.v12: Mas Deus é o nosso Rei

options.label: Mas Deus, o nosso Rei
options.note: Apposition, as MS1932; the colon then hangs until *operou*.

decisions.latin: Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare
decisions.why: The *confirmáre* row: *confirmar* where a word is confirmed, *firmar* where a thing or person is made firm (37:3, 40:13, 50:14). The sea made firm is the second. Douay-Rheims has *didst make the sea firm*, MS1932 *deste solidez ao mar*, and the Greek ἐκραταίωσας is 'made strong'. *in virtúte tua* → *com o vosso poder* (the *virtus* row; *com* for the instrument, as 64:7 *Vós que preparais os montes com o vosso poder*).

options.label: fortalecestes
options.note: The Greek's sense (MS1932 in the row).

decisions.latin: contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis
decisions.why: Two verbs of breaking heads, one in each verse: 73:13 *contribulásti* (συνέτριψας) and 73:14 *confregísti* (συνέθλασας). 73:14 keeps confríngere's row verb *quebrar*, so 73:13 needs another. *contribuláre → atribulado* (D44) belongs to the spirit of 50:19 and cannot crush a head. *esmagar* is the plain verb for crushing. MS1932's *pisaste* adds feet the Latin does not have.

decisions.latin: dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum
decisions.why: The enclitic after *destes* would be *deste-lo*, which is correct but stiff and looks like a *tu* form. *e o destes* supplies a conjunction the Latin lacks, which is grammar. *vós o destes* would add a seventh *vós* to the psalm's run of *Tu*, where the Latin has none in this colon. *esca → comida*: the row foresaw *alimento* or *comida* for food given, and *dar por comida* is MS1932's build. *Æthíopum* → *dos etíopes* (the people, as the Latin's genitive; MS1932 *da Etiópia*).

decisions.latin: tu fabricátus es auróram et solem
decisions.why: *fabricári* is the craftsman's verb ('to make out of wood, stone, metal; to frame, fashion', L&S). The Greek κατηρτίσω is 'framed, set in order'. The psalm uses four verbs of making in two verses (*fabricátus es, fecísti, plasmásti*), and they should stay apart. *fazer* is fécit's and *moldar* is plasmáre's (row, 118:73). *criar* (MS1932) is kept for *creáre* (50:12). *fabricar* keeps the Latin's image of a maker at work, at the cost of a factory's overtone.

decisions.latin: ánimas confiténtes tibi
decisions.why: *confitéri* to God → *dar graças a* (D5), with the dative kept. The Greek is ἐξομολογουμένην σοι, where the Hebrew has 'your turtledove': the Latin follows the Greek, and so does this. MS1932 has *que te louvam*, but *louvar* is laudáre's, which stands two verses later (73:21 *laudábunt*).

decisions.latin: quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum
decisions.why: Word for word: 'for they are filled, who have been darkened of the earth, with houses of iniquities'. The Greek is the same (οἱ ἐσκοτισμένοι τῆς γῆς οἴκων ἀνομιῶν). Douay-Rheims has *they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity*. MS1932 turns the persons into places (*todos os lugares obscuros do país*), which the Latin's masculine *qui* does not allow. The relative clause is condensed to a participle used as a noun, *os obscurecidos da terra*, which keeps its range (darkened, blinded, hidden, lowly). *repléti sunt* → *estão cheios* (the *replére* row, 64:10b). *domus → casa* (row); *iniquitátum* keeps its plural.

options.label: os que se obscureceram na terra

forms.obscurati: os que se obscureceram na terra

options.note: The relative clause kept; *terræ* made a place.

options.label: os lugares obscuros da terra
options.note: MS1932's places; not the Latin's persons. Refused.

decisions.latin: Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus
decisions.why: ἀποστραφήτω is to turn back, sent away. The pronominal *voltar-se* is used, as 69:4b (*Voltem-se*): bare *voltar* is heard as 'come back' (D44). *factus confúsus* ('made ashamed') → *envergonhado*: confúndi's word (D15), with *factus* carried by the participle. *confundido* (MS1932) is heard as 'confused' (D15). *húmilis → humilde* (D27). The natural order puts the subject first, after *Que*.

decisions.latin: eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die
decisions.why: 'of those which are from the fool all the day'. *vêm* is supplied for *sunt ab* (grammar). *são do insensato* says whose they are, where the Latin says where they come from. *das vossas afrontas* leaves the genitive *tuórum* open as the Latin does (the affronts done to you). Douay-Rheims explains it: *with which the foolish man hath reproached thee*. *tota die → o dia todo* (D24). *insípiens → insensato* (row), as 73:18.

options.label: das que são do insensato
options.note: The Latin's verb; heard as the fool's own affronts.

choices.73:1: *oves páscuæ tuæ → as ovelhas da vossa pastagem*, as the *páscua* row foresaw (78:13, 99:3b, 94:7 should agree). *super* → *contra* (ἐπί of hostility; DRB *against*). The verse opens the Introit of Pent13-0 as its psalm verse (missa/Latin/Tempora/Pent13-0.txt).
choices.73:2: Reads alone as the Thursday antiphon (with *Dómine*) and as the Preces versicle (*Meménto* for *Memor esto*); both halves stand alone. *Memor esto* → *Lembrai-vos de* (row; 118:49), the same at 73:18 and 73:22.
choices.73:2b: *in quo habitásti in eo* has a Hebrew-style resumptive pronoun ('in which you dwelt in it'). Portuguese cannot say it, so *em que habitastes* renders both. This is syntax, not a repetition the ear could keep. *mons Sion* is nominative, an exclamation in apposition, and stays so (*o monte Sião*, as 47:3).
choices.73:4: *gloriári* absolute → *se gloriaram* (row, 31:11 absolute; 51:3 the wicked man's boasting). *odérunt* → present *odeiam* (the *odísse* row), as 73:23.
choices.73:6: *a derrubaram*: the Latin's feminine *eam* has no stated antecedent (the doors? the forest *silva*? the house of God?), and the Portuguese *a* is just as open (*selva* is feminine too). Left so. *silva → selva* (D44). *lignórum → de árvores* (1:3a *lignum → árvore*). *excídere → cortar*, *dejícere → derrubar*: two verbs kept two.
choices.73:8: *Quiéscere faciámus → Façamos cessar* (DRB *abolish*, MS1932 *Façamos cessar*); *a terra → da terra*, put before the object so that it is not heard as *Deus da terra*. The Greek has 'let us burn' (κατακαύσωμεν), and the Latin is followed.
choices.73:10: The formula *Úsquequo … in finem?* → *Até quando … para sempre?* (D27), here with *Deus*. *adversárius → adversário*: new, and plain.
choices.73:13: The run of *Tu* (73:13, 14, 15 ×2, 16, 17 ×2) is kept exactly where the Latin has it, and nowhere else.
choices.73:15: *dirúmpere → romper* (row, 2:3). *fontes, et torréntes* without articles, as the Latin (*torrens → torrente*, row). *Ethan* is a proper name in the Latin and the Greek (Ηθαμ); the Hebrew איתן means 'ever-flowing', which the Latin did not read. Spelled *Etã*, the Portuguese form of the name.
choices.73:16: *Tuus est dies, et tua est nox* → *Vosso é o dia, e vossa é a noite*, the predicate first, as the Latin has it and as Portuguese allows.
choices.73:17: *términos terræ → os limites da terra* (row, 2:8; ὅρια here, not the πέρατα of 64:8 *os confins*). *plasmáre → moldar* (row, 118:73). The Latin's resumptive *ea* is kept (*vós os moldastes*).
choices.73:18: *Memor esto hujus* → *Lembrai-vos disto*. *pópulus insípiens* has no article in the Latin or the Greek (λαὸς ἄφρων), so *um povo insensato* (MS1932 the same).
choices.73:19: *béstiæ → feras* (the *oves / boves / pécora* row reserves *feras* for béstiæ). The Latin repeats *ánimas* in both colons, and so does the Portuguese. The Introit of Pent13-0 and the Gradual of Quad4-4 adapt this verse with 73:20 and 73:22 (*Réspice, Dómine, in testaméntum tuum … ne obliviscáris in finem*; grep).
choices.73:20: *Réspice in → Olhai para* (the formula *Réspice in me → Olhai para mim*). *testaméntum → aliança* (row).
choices.73:21: *pauper et inops → o pobre e o carente* (D38). *laudáre → louvar*.
choices.73:22: *Exsúrge, Deus → Levantai-vos, Deus* (row). *júdica causam tuam → julgai a vossa causa* (118:154 *a minha causa*).
choices.73:23: *voces inimicórum tuórum*: the Greek has 'your suppliants' (τῶν ἱκετῶν σου), and the Latin's enemies are followed. *ascéndit → sobe* (46:6 *Subiu Deus*); MS1932's *aumenta* interprets. *semper → sempre* (row).
choices.checks: Accepted soft flags: the length flags at 73:1b, 14b, 16a, 17b, 21b (+3/+4: Portuguese articles and the enclitic-free *e o destes*) and 73:22b, 23b (-6/-3: the Latin's long relative clause and genitive plural compress). The 73:10/73:11 rhyme is *para sempre* twice: the Latin's *in finem* twice, as the formula requires, so it is not a sought rhyme.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932; no Diurnal section for this psalm). Hard readings: 73:5 (*signa sua, signa … sicut in éxitu super summum*, the psalm's crux), 73:20 (*qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum*), 73:6 *in idípsum* (D9 deferred), and the three places of *improperáre*, a word found only in this psalm. Glossary rows applied: repéllere, in finem (D27), congregátio / synagóga (D34), possidére, virga, redímere, sanctum, malignári, gloriári, odísse, silva (D44), tabernáculum, simul, irritáre (D27), avértere, déxtera, operári (D43), confirmáre, confríngere, plasmáre, términi, insípiens, confitéri (D5), páscua, testaméntum, replére, domus, húmilis, inops (D38), exsúrgere, tota die (D24). Liturgical uses found by grep: the Thursday antiphon and the Preces versicle (73:2), and the Introit, Gradual and Alleluia of Pent13-0 / Quad4-4 (73:1, 19, 20, 22, adapted).
